name: BD handover to delivery
purpose: Transfer everything sold from BD to the delivery team: the signed SOW, proposal, estimates, assumptions, client context and promises made in sales calls, so delivery starts from what was actually agreed.
entryCriteria: Contract or SOW signed, or a signed letter of intent
Advance payment received or invoiced, per the contract
exitCriteria: Handover meeting held and recorded in a MoM
PM has read the SOW, proposal and estimate and listed open questions
Risky assumptions logged in the RAID log

raci.activity: Prepare handover pack (SOW, proposal, estimate, call notes)
Review SOW and list gaps or risky assumptions
Confirm commercial model, milestones and payment terms

clientTouchpoints: Introduction email from BD naming the PM
Optional short intro call before the formal kickoff
typicalDuration: Typically 1–3 working days after signature
pitfalls: Verbal promises made in sales calls that are not in the SOW
PM starting without reading the SOW
Assumptions that the client never actually agreed to

name: Estimation & commercial model
purpose: Produce or validate the effort estimate and confirm the commercial model (fixed bid, T&M, retainer or dedicated team), milestones and billing, so the plan and the price rest on the same assumptions.
exitCriteria: Estimate reviewed by the tech lead with assumptions and exclusions
Milestones and milestone billing mapped to deliverables

raci.activity: Break scope into features and estimate effort

typicalDuration: Typically 2–10 working days, depending on the size and clarity of scope
pitfalls: Estimating from a one-line brief
No written exclusions
Milestones that bill before anything verifiable is delivered
Ignoring QA, PM and store-review time

name: Internal kickoff
purpose: Align the delivery team on goals, scope, team roles, plan, risks, environments and ways of working before meeting the client.
entryCriteria: SOW and estimate available to the team
exitCriteria: Team understands scope and out-of-scope items
Draft plan, RACI and RAID log ready

raci.activity: Request repositories, environments and tool access

typicalDuration: Typically 1–2 working days
pitfalls: Skipping it because the team is 'already busy'
Team not told what is out of scope
Risks discovered only after the client kickoff

name: Client kickoff
purpose: Start the engagement with the client: introduce teams, confirm goals, scope, plan, communication cadence, SPOCs, escalation path and the client's dependencies.
entryCriteria: Kickoff agenda shared with the client in advance
exitCriteria: MoM sent with confirmed SPOCs, cadence and next steps

raci.activity: Confirm goals, scope and success criteria
Name SPOCs and agree communication cadence

typicalDuration: Typically a 60–90 minute meeting within the first week
pitfalls: No client decision-maker present
Not stating client dependencies and their dates
Leaving cadence and SPOC vague

name: Discovery & requirements
purpose: Turn the agreed scope into detailed, testable requirements (BRD or PRD, user stories with acceptance criteria) and get them frozen and signed off before build.
exitCriteria: User stories with acceptance criteria written
Open questions closed or logged as assumptions
typicalDuration: Typically 1–4 weeks, depending on project size
pitfalls: Writing stories without acceptance criteria
Accepting 'we'll decide later' on core flows
No written sign-off, only verbal agreement
New requirements added after freeze without a CR

sources.label: GOV.UK Service Manual: How the discovery phase works
GOV.UK Service Manual: Writing user stories

name: UI/UX & design approval
purpose: Design wireframes, mockups and prototypes for the agreed flows and get the client's design approval within the agreed revision rounds.
entryCriteria: Requirements signed off or stable for the screens being designed
typicalDuration: Typically 1–4 weeks, often overlapping with discovery
pitfalls: Unlimited revision rounds
Approval from someone other than the SPOC
Design changes after approval treated as free

name: Architecture & Sprint 0
purpose: Set up the foundations before feature sprints: architecture decisions, repositories, environments, CI/CD, coding standards, backlog and definition of ready and done.
entryCriteria: Requirements and designs stable enough to plan
exitCriteria: Backlog refined for the first sprints
Definition of ready and done agreed

raci.activity: Set up repositories, environments and CI/CD
Refine backlog and plan first sprint
Agree definition of ready and done

clientTouchpoints: Optional architecture walkthrough with the client's technical team
typicalDuration: Typically 1–2 weeks
pitfalls: Skipping Sprint 0 and fixing environments mid-project
Undocumented architecture decisions
No staging environment for client review

sources.label: GOV.UK Service Manual: How the alpha phase works

name: Sprint execution
purpose: Build the product in short iterations: plan each sprint, develop and test, demo to the client, take feedback, and report progress transparently.
entryCriteria: Backlog items meet the definition of ready
exitCriteria: All planned scope built and tested to the definition of done
Sprint demos held and feedback triaged

raci.activity: Demo to client and collect feedback
Send status report and EOD updates

typicalDuration: Typically 2-week sprints, repeated until the scope is built
pitfalls: Treating demo feedback as free changes
Hiding slippage behind a green RAG
QA left until the end

name: Scope control: CR, enhancement, bug
purpose: Classify every new client request as a bug, enhancement, change request, new feature or clarification, and handle it with the right process and billing before work starts.
entryCriteria: A new request arrives from the client
Scope baseline and acceptance criteria exist
exitCriteria: CRs estimated, priced and approved in writing before work

raci.activity: Estimate impact on time and cost

typicalDuration: Typically ongoing through delivery; each CR typically takes 1–5 working days to estimate and approve
pitfalls: Starting CR work before written approval
Calling a change 'small' and absorbing it
Classifying a missed requirement as a CR, or a CR as a bug

name: QA, UAT & sign-off
purpose: Verify the product internally (QA, regression, smoke tests), then let the client validate it against the acceptance criteria in UAT and give written UAT sign-off.
entryCriteria: Build feature-complete on the UAT environment
Internal QA passed with no open blockers
Test cases and UAT scenarios ready
exitCriteria: UAT feedback triaged into bugs, CRs and clarifications
typicalDuration: Typically 1–3 weeks
pitfalls: UAT feedback containing new features accepted as bugs
Open-ended UAT with no end date
Go-live without written sign-off

sources.label: GOV.UK Service Manual: How the beta phase works

name: Release & go-live
purpose: Deploy to production and make the product available to users in a controlled way: go/no-go decision, cutover, store submission for apps, smoke test and rollback plan.
entryCriteria: Production environment and client-owned accounts ready
exitCriteria: Apps approved and published where relevant

raci.activity: Prepare go-live checklist and rollback plan

typicalDuration: Typically 1–5 working days, plus store review time for mobile apps
pitfalls: Releasing on a Friday evening or before a holiday
No tested rollback plan
Store accounts not ready in the client's name

sources.label: GOV.UK Service Manual: Deploying software regularly

name: Hypercare & warranty
purpose: Watch the live product closely right after go-live, fix launch issues fast, and handle warranty claims for defects against the agreed scope.
exitCriteria: Launch issues resolved or moved to support
Hypercare log reviewed with the client
clientTouchpoints: Daily or frequent check-ins in the first days
typicalDuration: Typically 1–4 weeks of hypercare; warranty typically 30–90 days after go-live
pitfalls: Treating new requests as warranty bugs
No clear end of hypercare
Hotfixes deployed without approval or testing

name: Handover & KT
purpose: Hand over source code, credentials, documentation and knowledge so the client or its next team can own and operate the product.
entryCriteria: Final payment received or as per the contract
exitCriteria: Source code and assets handed over as per the contract
Credentials transferred and agency access reviewed

raci.activity: Hand over code, documentation and credentials

typicalDuration: Typically 1–2 weeks
pitfalls: Handing over code before payment terms are met
Credentials kept in personal accounts
No recorded KT

name: Support, AMC & retainers
purpose: Run the product after warranty under an agreed support model (AMC, retainer, T&M support), with SLAs for response and resolution.
entryCriteria: Warranty ended or support contract signed
exitCriteria: Monthly or quarterly support reports sent
typicalDuration: Typically ongoing, on monthly or yearly terms
pitfalls: Doing support work with no active plan
No record of hours used under a retainer
Letting the plan expire without a renewal conversation

sources.label: GOV.UK Service Manual: How the live phase works

name: Closure
purpose: Formally close the project: confirm all deliverables and payments, run a retrospective, write the closure report, archive the project and identify follow-on opportunities.
exitCriteria: Case study or referral asked for where appropriate

raci.activity: Ask for feedback, testimonial or next phase

typicalDuration: Typically 1–2 weeks
pitfalls: Projects that never formally close
Lessons learned not shared with other PMs
Forgetting to remove access

name: Demo & requirement call
purpose: Show the client the white-label product as it is, and capture what it needs: brand, markets, languages, payment and messaging providers, and any gaps from the standard product.
exitCriteria: Demo given and recorded in a MoM
typicalDuration: Typically 1–2 calls within a week
pitfalls: Promising features the core does not have
Not asking about payment gateways and countries early
Demo on a broken or outdated environment

name: Gap analysis
purpose: Classify each client need as out of the box, configuration or customisation, and estimate and price the customisations before setup starts.
clientTouchpoints: Written approval of scope and quote
typicalDuration: Typically 2–7 working days
pitfalls: Accepting customisations inside core files
Calling customisations 'configuration' to close the sale
No written approval of gaps

sources.label: Microsoft Learn: Tenancy models for a multitenant solution

name: Collecting the brand kit
purpose: Collect all brand assets and content needed for rebranding in the right formats and sizes.
entryCriteria: Brand-kit checklist sent to the client
exitCriteria: All brand assets received and checked
App names and listing texts confirmed
typicalDuration: Typically 3–10 working days, depending on the client
pitfalls: Low-resolution logos
Missing dark-mode or icon variants
Assets arriving after builds start

name: Client-owned accounts
purpose: Make sure the client opens and owns every account the product needs (Apple, Google Play, hosting, domain, payment, messaging) and grants Oyelabs the right access.
exitCriteria: All accounts active in the client's name
Keys shared through a secure channel

raci.activity: Verify access and record in instance register

typicalDuration: Typically 1–3 weeks, mainly waiting for store and payment verification
pitfalls: Starting Apple organisation enrolment late
Accounts opened in a freelancer's or agency's name
Keys shared over chat or email

sources.label: Apple Developer Program: Enrol (individuals and organisations)
Play Console Help: Add developer account users and manage permissions

name: Configuration & custom modules
purpose: Set up the client instance: apply theme and branding, configure business settings, switch on features and build approved custom modules as separate modules.
exitCriteria: Approved custom modules built and tested

raci.activity: Set up instance and apply branding

typicalDuration: Typically 1–3 weeks, longer with custom modules
pitfalls: Customisation creeping in as 'small tweaks'
Undocumented configuration values
Custom code written into core files

sources.label: Martin Fowler: Feature Toggles (aka Feature Flags)

name: Rebranded builds, QA & UAT
purpose: Produce the rebranded app builds and panels, test them for branding and configuration correctness and regression, and get the client's UAT sign-off.
entryCriteria: Bundle ID and package name set
typicalDuration: Typically 1–2 weeks
pitfalls: Demo product name or logo left in a screen or email
Wrong bundle ID or package name
UAT feedback that is really customisation

sources.label: GOV.UK Service Manual: How the beta phase works

name: Store listing preparation
purpose: Prepare store listings and compliance details: app names, descriptions, screenshots, privacy policy URL, privacy declarations, age ratings and review notes.
exitCriteria: Privacy policy live on the client's domain
Review notes and demo credentials ready
typicalDuration: Typically 3–7 working days
pitfalls: Placeholder or copied descriptions
Privacy policy that does not match data collected
No demo credentials for the reviewer

sources.label: App Store Connect Help: Screenshot specifications
Play Console Help: Add preview assets to showcase your app

name: Submission, rejection & resubmission
purpose: Submit the apps for store review, track the review, respond to rejections and resubmit until approved.
exitCriteria: Apps approved by Apple and Google
Rejections logged with cause and fix
typicalDuration: Typically 2–7 days, longer if rejected
pitfalls: Submitting from an agency account (Guideline 4.2.6 risk)
Arguing with the reviewer instead of fixing
Not telling the client a launch date depends on review

sources.label: App Store Connect Help: Overview of submitting for review

name: Go-live, licence & support plan
purpose: Launch the client instance and apps, start the licence or subscription, and put the support plan and escalation path in place.
entryCriteria: Setup fee paid as per the contract
exitCriteria: Support plan, SLA and escalation matrix shared

raci.activity: Release apps and switch on production

typicalDuration: Typically 1–3 working days
pitfalls: Going live before payment terms are met
Client admins never trained
No agreed support channel

name: Core product upgrades
purpose: Keep each client instance on a supported core version: plan, test and roll out core upgrades, and manage custom modules and merge conflicts.
entryCriteria: Instance register shows which clients need it

raci.activity: Assess upgrade impact on custom modules

clientTouchpoints: Quote for customisation impact if any
typicalDuration: Typically hours to days per instance; longer for heavily customised or forked instances
pitfalls: Instances left many versions behind
Customisation impact discovered mid-upgrade
Store SDK deadlines missed
